survey: A cream refractor telescope tube runs diagonally from a small grey eyepiece at the lower left, through a gold ring and grey collar, to a wider dew-shield end with a blue objective lens at the upper right. The tube sits in a grey yoke bracket with a round pivot bolt. The bracket stands on a small grey base plate on a round wooden tripod head. Three wooden legs splay out from under the head: one toward the viewer, one to the right and one to the back left. Each leg ends in a grey cap foot that rests on cratered grey lunar ground, with soft shadows falling back and to the right. The camera is slightly above the object. We see the top of the wooden head and of the base plate, and the craters are flat ellipses, which suits a low, slightly raised view. The legs, feet, shadows and ground agree with each other, and the feet sit on the ground believably.

errors.where: Objective lens end of the tube (upper right) compared with the tube body and the yoke pivot bolt
errors.what: The lens face is drawn as a fairly open ellipse, so the front of the tube seems to point well toward the viewer. But the tube body barely changes in width along its length, and the pivot bolt on the yoke is a front-on circle, which places the tube's swing axis pointing straight at the camera. With that bolt, the tube should lie nearly flat across the picture and the lens would be seen almost edge-on. The lens opening and the rest of the tube suggest two different camera angles.

The eyepiece cap also shows its rounded end toward the viewer. If the objective end comes toward the camera, the eyepiece end goes away from it, so its end face should be hidden. A cylinder cannot show both of its end faces at once.

errors.where: Tripod head and base plate compared with the horizon
errors.what: The horizon line sits at about the height of the tripod head, which reads as eye level. Even so, the tops of the wooden disc and the base plate are drawn clearly from above. A flat disc at eye level would look almost edge-on. This is mild, and many viewers would accept it as stylization.

fix: Use one consistent three-quarter view from slightly above. The telescope tube angles up and slightly toward the viewer and gets visibly wider toward the near objective end. The objective lens is a narrow ellipse that matches the tube's angle. The eyepiece end at the far lower left shows only its side, with no end face visible. The yoke pivot bolt is drawn as an ellipse at right angles to the tube, not as a front-on circle. Place the horizon a little above the tripod head, so that the top faces of the wooden head and the base plate are seen from just above.
